Package dev.opencollab.paletter.item

Class ItemOverride

java.lang.Object
dev.opencollab.paletter.item.ItemOverride
@Experimental public final class ItemOverride extends Object
Changes to a vanilla (or earlier layer's) item definition, applied in a layer. Received in PaletteLayer.Builder.overrideItem(java.lang.String, java.util.function.Consumer<dev.opencollab.paletter.item.ItemOverride>); anything not set keeps its current value. 

 // Bedrock stacks cakes to 64, Java to 1
 layer.overrideItem("minecraft:cake", item -> item.modifyComponents(MaxStackSize.of(1)));
 // Like a BDS add-on for a data driven item: only these components are left (the apple keeps its creative category)
 layer.overrideItem("minecraft:apple", item -> item.replaceComponents(MaxStackSize.of(3)));
 // Make the firework rocket data driven and merge onto its current data; whether that stops the client's
 // own firework boosting is unverified on a client
 layer.overrideItem("minecraft:firework_rocket", item -> item.version(ItemVersion.DATA_DRIVEN).modifyComponents(MaxStackSize.of(64)));

Experimental. BDS overrides of a vanilla data driven item (such as minecraft:apple, format 1.26.60) replace the vanilla components (replaceComponents(dev.opencollab.paletter.item.component.ItemComponent...)). For hard coded items BDS accepted minecraft:feather at format 1.10 (it became a legacy item, id kept) and rejected minecraft:stick at 1.26.60; a legacy minecraft:bread at 1.16.100 was rejected, asking for 1.20.0 or higher, which was never tried. Paletter does not refuse any override. How the Bedrock client treats Paletter's overrides is unverified on a client: no client test exists. Paletter also keeps every vanilla runtime id fixed, where BDS moves an overridden data driven item. This API may change.

Since:
1.0.0

    • modifyComponents

      public @NonNull ItemOverride modifyComponents(@NonNull ItemComponent... components)
      Merges components onto the item's current component data: what they write replaces the original keys (including single item_properties entries), everything else is sent as before. Marks the item component based.

      BDS never produces this shape: an add-on override replaces the vanilla components, see replaceComponents(dev.opencollab.paletter.item.component.ItemComponent...). The client's behaviour for a merged vanilla item is unverified.

      Parameters:
      components - the components to merge; a later component replaces an earlier one of the same name
      Returns:
      this override

    • replaceComponents

      public @NonNull ItemOverride replaceComponents(@NonNull ItemComponent... components)
      Replaces the item's components with only these (the custom item defaults underneath), like a BDS add-on that overrides a vanilla data driven item. The vanilla item_properties.creative_category is kept, as BDS does. Also forces the item data driven and component based, and discards the components of earlier modifyComponents(dev.opencollab.paletter.item.component.ItemComponent...) calls. Whether the client then stops applying hard coded behaviour is unverified on a client.

      BDS accepted this for the data driven apple; for a hard coded item it rejected the stick (1.26.60) and accepted the feather only as a legacy item (1.10). Paletter applies it to any item (unverified on a client). Unlike BDS, the runtime id stays the vanilla one.

      Parameters:
      components - the only components the item has, apart from the custom item defaults
      Returns:
      this override
